privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.notice: This invitation site uses only the information needed to manage wedding invitations, replies, and song requests.

collection.title: Information collected
collection.body: The private invitation link identifies your invitation. If you reply, the site stores your attendance, guest count and additional guest names, language, and any dietary requirements or note you provide. Song requests may include a title, artist, and optional Spotify link. Limited invitation events record the invitation identifier, event type, time, locale, and session identifier.

purpose.title: Why and who can access it
purpose.body: Ruben and Andrea use this information to organize the wedding and manage replies. They are the only people authorized to view guest information in the private admin area. It is not shared with other guests or used for advertising. The hosting and database providers may process it as needed to operate and secure the site. Please keep your invitation link private.

services.title: Service providers
services.body: The site's hosting provider and Supabase store and process information to run the invitation and database. They do not use guest details for their own advertising. The embedded map loads OpenStreetMap tiles when you reach the venue section; your browser connects directly to OpenStreetMap, which may receive technical request data such as your IP address under its privacy policy. Apple Maps and Google Maps links open those services if you choose them. The Spotify player loads automatically when the Music section comes into view, and your browser connects directly to Spotify to display it. Spotify also receives song searches and selected track requests through the site's server so requested songs can be added to the wedding playlist.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: After the wedding and the related follow-up are complete, Ruben and Andrea will delete the guest, RSVP, dietary, song-request, and invitation-event information from the wedding database. Technical backups may remain temporarily under the service providers' retention schedules before they are removed.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: To view, correct, or delete your information, contact Ruben and Andrea directly through the channel you normally use to reach them. Include the name shown on your invitation so they can find the right record.

travel.label: Getting around
travel.title: Getting to Vienna and getting around
travel.originInfo: From Madrid, direct flights to Vienna (VIE) are operated by Ryanair and Iberia; from Barcelona, direct routes are available with Vueling and Austrian Airlines. From Caracas, Iberia connects via Madrid (MAD) directly to Vienna. Flight schedules may shift seasonally: if booking separate legs, allow ample time for luggage retrieval and re-checking.
travel.airportInfo: From Vienna Airport (VIE), regular ÖBB trains offer the best value: the S7 S-Bahn takes 25 minutes to Wien Mitte and the Railjet express connects in 15 minutes to Wien Hauptbahnhof (standard single fare ~€4.40, or ~€2.20 supplement if you already hold a Vienna city pass). The City Airport Train (CAT) reaches Wien Mitte in 21 minutes for €14.90 one way (€24.90 return; children under 15 travel free); due to rail modernization works scheduled through 31 October 2027, the CAT is temporarily running as a dedicated express bus ('CAT by bus') and City Check-in is paused. The airport lies outside the city zone, requiring an outer zone ticket.
travel.cityTicketInfo: Vienna's U-Bahn, trams, and buses share the same core-zone network. A digital single ticket costs €3.00 via the official WienMobil app (€3.20 at ticket machines) and covers one journey with unlimited transfers; the 24-hour pass is €10.20 (Wiener Linien discontinued the former 48h and 72h tickets in its 2026 fare reform). Digital tickets are tied to your name and can be purchased easily on your smartphone.
travel.priceNote: Fares and transit conditions verified for 2026/2027 following official Wiener Linien, ÖBB, and CAT tariff structures. Schedules and prices may fluctuate; please re-check via official links closer to your departure.

dress.label: What to wear
dress.title: Dress code
dress.formality: Formal attire · Austrian imperial court style with a modern twist.
dress.subtitle: We are celebrating in an authentic Viennese baroque palace! Dress to impress the Habsburg royalty: elegant tuxedos, sharp dark suits, and glamorous floor-length gowns or chic formal cocktail dresses. Rich royal tones, velvet fabrics, and imperial flair are warmly encouraged.
dress.decree: Empress Andrea's Royal Decree: Tiaras and royal touches are highly celebrated — sneakers are strictly subject to imperial pardon!
dress.footwearDescription: Historic Viennese palace courtyards feature authentic cobblestones that can challenge delicate stilettos. Block heels, elegant dressy wedges, or chic flats will keep you reigning comfortably on the dance floor all night.
dress.weatherDescription: Early October in Vienna brings crisp, romantic imperial autumn air (around 16–18°C by day, cooling to 10–12°C after dusk). An elegant shawl, royal cape, tailored blazer, or evening jacket is strongly recommended for palace garden strolls and outdoor transitions.

closing.label: With love
closing.title: We cannot wait to celebrate with you
closing.message: Thank you for being part of our lives. We are looking forward to sharing this day with you.
closing.story:
If you’re reading this, consider yourself part of a very special group of people that Ruben, Andrea, or both of us have chosen to celebrate one of the most important days of our lives with.

It may have taken us a while to find each other, but once we did, we were immediately inseparable. If you’ve spent time with us during these almost two years, you probably already know how happy we are together.

We would truly love to have you there to celebrate with us. In one way or another, you’ve been part of our lives, and we treasure the memories and moments we’ve shared with you.

If you live in Europe, you have very few excuses. If you’re coming from Venezuela or another part of the world, please don’t feel pressured — we completely understand that such a long trip isn’t always possible, and we love you either way.

But if you can make it, come ready to eat, drink, dance and celebrate. We’ll do our best to make it an unforgettable day for all of us.

Ruben & Andrea
